blurb: Every repo and skill from the 3 November issue, with what each does and the setup steps from its own README.
intro: Issue #36 had six repos and four AI skills, and this page covers nine of them. Most of it is for builders: desktop computer use for agents, huge local models on ordinary hardware, co-op mods for single-player games, and skills for AI search visibility, plainer writing and smaller images. If you want to run a big model at home, start with colibri. If you write with AI help, try ce-noslop.

items.name: agent-desktop
items.works_with: Any coding agent through the CLI, MCP or a skill; macOS, Windows and Linux
items.short: A computer use CLI that lets your AI agent read and operate desktop apps through the accessibility tree, with no screenshots.
items.what: agent-desktop reads a desktop app's accessibility tree and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check, and repeats. It has no model inside; the loop lives in your agent. It ships as a CLI, an MCP server and a C library.
items.who: Developers who want an agent to drive native desktop apps on macOS, Windows or Linux. You need your own agent to run the loop.
needs: Node.js with npm (or Bun, Yarn, pnpm), or Homebrew on macOS and Linux
macOS 13 or later, Windows 10 1809 or later, or Ubuntu 24.04 or later
On macOS: the Accessibility permission

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: On macOS and Linux, `brew install agent-desktop` also works.

steps.title: Check your setup
steps.text: On macOS the second command walks you through the Accessibility grant.

steps.title: Or add it as an MCP server
steps.text: Every command becomes an MCP tool, such as `desktop_snapshot` and `desktop_click`.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i` to list Finder's interactive elements with refs, click one with `agent-desktop click` and its ref, then snapshot again to check.

watch: It needs accessibility access, which lets it read and operate every app on your desktop.
Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots and debug files can contain private desktop content. The README says to keep them out of public logs and uploads.
Actions are headless by default, with no pointer movement or focus change. `--headed` uses real input.
In PowerShell, quote every ref, because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator.

items.name: Craft Anything
items.cost: Free (MIT or Apache 2.0). Building uses your own coding agent sign-in
items.works_with: Claude Code first; Copilot CLI and other ACP agents partly; MCP clients
items.short: Studies how a website, app or game works, then has a coding agent build your own version and checks it against the original.
items.what: You point it at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It studies the original with real inspection tools, has a coding agent build a new project in the stack you name, compares the result with the original, and refines it. A Clean room mode, the default, works only from what a visitor can see; Deep mode also reads the code and files. All 320 tools are also CLI commands and MCP tools.
items.who: Builders who want to learn how something is made or rebuild a layout or game idea in their own stack. It is early alpha, so expect rough edges.
needs: A coding agent signed in on your computer, with Claude Code supported first
To build from source: Rust 1.97 or newer, and on Debian or Ubuntu some desktop libraries
Optional: Ghidra for Deep mode, a fal.ai key for generated pictures and 3D models

steps.title: Download it
steps.text: Installers for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD are on the latest release page, with a `SHA256SUMS` file: https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/latest

steps.title: Or build it from source
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything && cd craft-anything
cargo run --release -p craft-anything                # the desktop app
cargo install --path apps/craft-anything-cli         # the CLI, as `craft-anything-cli`

steps.title: Check the install
steps.text: It checks the install, your coding agents and the engines, and says what is missing.

steps.title: Make something
steps.text: In the app, pick a website, app or game, describe what you want and press Start. New projects go in `Documents/Craft Anything`.

watch: The project says to use it only on software you own or are allowed to examine. It does not bypass DRM, logins or anti-cheat.
Clean room is a rule about which tools it offers, not a sandbox. Your coding agent still acts as you with its own permissions.
Installing a build's dependencies runs code on your computer. Only choose "always allow" for npm on projects whose packages you trust.
It is early alpha. Building with API keys and agents other than Claude Code is not yet run live.

items.name: colibri
items.cost: Free (Apache 2.0). Each model keeps its own licence
items.works_with: Linux, macOS, Windows; OpenAI and Anthropic compatible API for other apps
items.short: Runs huge mixture-of-experts models on the computer you already have by keeping experts on disk. Pure C, no GPU needed.
items.what: A mixture-of-experts model uses only a small part of itself for each token. colibri keeps that part in RAM and reads the rest, the experts, from disk when the model asks for them. It runs thirteen engines today, including GLM-5.2, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Flash and Qwen3.6, on the CPU, on any GPU through Vulkan, or on NVIDIA through CUDA. A one-step setup picks a model that fits your machine and opens a dashboard.
items.who: People who want to run big open models on ordinary hardware and can wait for long downloads. The setup recommends a model that fits your RAM and disk.
needs: At least 8 GB of RAM (16 GB or more is better)
22 GB free on the disk for the smallest model, and an internet connection
Git, Python 3 and a C compiler (on macOS, Xcode tools and Homebrew)
A GPU is optional

steps.title: On Windows
steps.text: On the repo page click Code, then Download ZIP, and unzip it. Double-click `START-HERE.bat`. If Python is missing, it offers to install it.

steps.title: On Linux (Ubuntu and Debian)
steps.code:
sudo apt install git python3 build-essential
git clone https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri
cd colibri
./start-here.sh

steps.title: On macOS
steps.code:
xcode-select --install
brew install libomp git python
git clone https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri
cd colibri
./start-here.sh

steps.title: Pick a model
steps.text: You answer one question, which model, and Enter takes the recommendation. It downloads with resume, starts colibri and opens the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8000/. Add `--list` to see every model against your machine.

steps.title: Next time
steps.text: Run the same script again and it starts straight away. `c/coli status` shows what is installed and `c/coli stop` stops it.

try.label: From the README
try.text: `./coli chat` to talk to the model in the terminal, or point another app at the OpenAI base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`.

watch: Models are big. The smallest needs 22 GB of disk, and GLM-5.2 is a 429 GB download.
Each model keeps its own licence. The README notes Qwen-Image-2.1 is for non-commercial use only.
On WSL, keep the models on the Linux disk. The README says `/mnt/c` is many times slower.
The README offers a prompt for your coding assistant to run the setup. Its guide tells the assistant to ask before downloading a model or installing a system package.

items.name: AnyModelBot
items.cost: Free app (MIT). Models are pay per use through a Modelflare account
items.works_with: Windows, macOS, Linux, Docker; WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, Slack, Discord
items.short: A local-first app for your own AI bots on GPT, Claude, Gemini and 70+ models, reachable from chat apps and able to run tasks in the background.
items.what: Each bot has its own persona, default model, workspace and memory. You chat with it in the app or from WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, Slack or Discord, and it can read and write files, run commands, operate your desktop and run scheduled rules in the background. Every model comes through Modelflare, a paid gateway, and conversations, memory, files and keys stay on your device.
items.who: People who want an always-on personal AI agent they run themselves, with one bill across many models. Skip it if you want to use your own provider keys directly, since models come from Modelflare.
needs: A Modelflare account with credit
For Docker: a NAS or server with Docker
To build from source: Node.js 22.13+ and Go 1.26.8+

steps.title: Download the app
steps.text: Pick the installer for Windows, macOS or Linux from the releases page: https://github.com/modelflare-ai/AnyModelBot/releases. On Linux, `chmod +x` the AppImage and run it.

steps.title: Check the download
steps.text: Compare it with the line in the release's `SHA256SUMS`. On macOS use `shasum -a 256 <file>`.

steps.title: Sign in to Modelflare
steps.text: The first launch opens your browser to sign in or sign up. The app then connects itself, so there is no key to copy.

steps.title: Or run it in Docker
steps.text: Then open `http://<host>:3600/?token=<token>`.
steps.code:
docker run -d --name amb -p 3600:3600 -v amb-data:/data ghcr.io/modelflare-ai/anymodel-bot
docker exec amb cat /data/ui-token

try.label: From the README
try.text: "Every morning at 8, check X's price and tell me if it drops below 200." Say "observe first" to see what it would do before it acts.

watch: Model requests go through Modelflare to the provider you pick, and Modelflare keeps request logs. Its Trust Center says what is kept and for how long.
Bots can run commands and operate your desktop. Computer use runs automatically by default; switch a bot to ask before changing the screen if you want to approve each action.
Image and video generation asks first only above an estimated 0.50 US dollars. Tasks and rules have default budgets you can change.
Task folders unused for 30 days are deleted without asking unless you press Keep.
Don't expose port 3600 directly to the internet.

items.name: Co-op Anything
items.cost: Free (MIT). Everyone needs their own copy of the game
items.works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode; Steam
items.short: An MCP server and playbook that points your coding agent at a single-player game to make it co-op with friends.
items.what: You tell your agent which game you want to play together. It checks a directory of 230+ co-op mods, then either revives a buggy or abandoned mod or reverse engineers the game to build co-op from zero. It tests the result with bots in real game clients and packages it so friends install it in one click and join over Steam without port forwarding.
items.who: PC gamers with patience and a coding agent who want to play a single-player game with friends. The README says you don't need to code, but a game with no existing mod can take many agent hours.
needs: A coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor or OpenCode
The game installed for every player
Python, for the MCP server

steps.title: Tell your agent what you want
steps.text: Swap in your game.
steps.code:
Read https://github.com/cranebeaker/coop-anything and follow AGENTS.md.
I want to play <game> in co-op with my friends.

steps.title: Add the MCP server
steps.text: It searches the co-op directory, detects a game's engine and validates contributions. Claude Code picks it up from the repo's `.mcp.json`; for other agents, with your clone's path:

steps.title: Check the directory first
steps.text: Browse coopanything.app or `DIRECTORY.md`. If a co-op mod already exists, the README says most projects take days at most.

try.label: From the README
try.text: "Read https://github.com/cranebeaker/coop-anything and follow AGENTS.md. I want to play <game> in co-op with my friends."

watch: The quick start has your agent follow the repo's own AGENTS.md and skills. Read them first so you know what it will do.
Building from zero means reverse engineering, DLL hooks and tools like Ghidra and debuggers. The README says the agent asks before installing anything or using your accounts.
The Steam relay uses Valve's free Spacewar test app.
Your agent opens a draft pull request back to the repo with what it learned. You review and publish it.
The project rules forbid anything that cheats in other people's multiplayer games or touches anti-cheat.

items.name: BLA
items.works_with: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Antigravity, OpenCode, VS Code, Copilot CLI
items.short: Hardens the builds you ship so AI reverse-engineering agents hit limits and chase decoys, while your app runs the same.
items.what: BLA (Blind LLM Agents) targets REA, an AI reverse-engineering agent. It plants format-valid decoys and canaries in your release artifacts and pads them past REA's documented resource limits, so the analyzer fails or burns tokens. It covers JavaScript, Electron, WASM, SQLite, Python, model files and more, and checks that the protected build behaves the same as the original.
items.who: Developers who ship JavaScript, Electron, WASM or model files and worry about AI-assisted copying. The project says it is defensive and for your own software only.
needs: Node.js ^22.23.4 or 24.x
A coding agent, if you want the skill and MCP setup
Optional: Wabt and tshark, for the red-team tests

steps.title: Register it with your coding agent
steps.text: This sets up the MCP server and the bundled skill.

steps.title: Harden your project
steps.text: It finds `dist/`, `build/`, `.asar`, `.wasm`, `.sqlite` and model files, then runs audit, protect and verify.

steps.title: Or ask your agent
steps.text: After setup, the skill guides a one-click harden.

steps.title: See the benchmark
steps.text: A 14-target showcase with estimated token multipliers and measured runtime checks.

watch: Hardened files can grow a lot. In the README's own runs an Electron `.asar` went from 607 B to 16.9 MiB and a WASM file from 54 B to 6.56 MiB.
It adds decoy credentials and fake diagnostic paths to your build, and a runtime guard that returns fake telemetry when it detects debugging tools. Test the build before you ship it.
LLM-facing bait such as fake notices and in-band AI chat markers is off by default. `--llm-directives` turns it on.
Results are verified against REA only. The README says it does not claim the same against Ghidra, Frida, JADX and similar tools.
The token and cost multipliers in the benchmark are internal estimates.

items.name: geo-optimizer
items.cost: Free (MIT). The `citations` command uses your own AI provider API key
items.works_with: Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf and other MCP clients; any shell
items.short: Audits your site for whether AI search engines can find and cite it, scores it 0 to 100 and previews the fixes.
items.what: The skill drives the `geo` command line tool. `geo audit` scores a site 0 to 100 across 9 categories for ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overviews, with a list of fixes in order. `geo fix` previews changes to robots.txt AI crawler rules, llms.txt, JSON-LD schema and meta tags, and writes them only when you add `--apply`.
items.who: Site owners and marketers who rank on Google but want to show up in AI answers. A good audit makes a site eligible; the skill says it does not guarantee a citation.
needs: Python 3.10 or later
The `geo` tool, version 4.19.10 or later
For the Claude Code plugin: `uv` on your PATH
Optional, for `geo citations`: an API key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Perplexity, Gemini, DeepSeek or another listed provider

steps.title: Install the geo tool
steps.text: The skill stops if `geo` is missing, so do this first.
steps.code: pipx install geo-optimizer-skill          # or: pip install geo-optimizer-skill

steps.title: Install the skill in Claude Code
steps.text: This installs the skill and the MCP server, but not the `geo` tool itself.

steps.title: Or add just the MCP server
steps.code:
pip install "geo-optimizer-skill[mcp]"
claude mcp add geo-optimizer -- geo-mcp

steps.title: Preview the fixes
steps.text: Nothing is written until you add `--apply`.

try.label: From the README
try.where: Your coding agent, with the MCP server added
try.text: "Audit my site and fix what's missing."

watch: `geo citations` sends your query texts to the AI or search API you configure and spends your API credit. The skill tells the agent to ask you first.
`geo audit` loads every installed audit plugin unless you pass `--no-plugins`.
`geo schema --inject` edits the HTML file you name, after saving a `.bak` copy.
History is kept in `~/.geo-optimizer/tracking.db`, and records older than 90 days are deleted.
The project says `geo` has no telemetry or update check.

items.name: ce-noslop
items.works_with: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and 11 more agent hosts
items.short: Checks or rewrites your writing so it has no AI tells and reads plainly, while keeping every fact from the source.
items.what: ce-noslop has three modes. Edit rewrites only the sentences that fail its tests, detect names each pattern and quotes the line without rewriting, and author holds the tests while you or the agent draft. Its seven tests ask, for each sentence, whether it states a fact about this project, names who acts and makes sense on the first read. It never adds facts and leaves code blocks, quotes and links alone.
items.who: Anyone who writes docs, READMEs, release notes or reports with AI help and wants them plainer. It comes inside Compound Engineering, a plugin of 37 skills, so you get the rest too.
needs: A supported agent host such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex

steps.title: Or in Cursor
steps.text: In Cursor Agent chat:

steps.title: Or in Codex CLI
steps.text: Restart Codex after the install finishes.
steps.code:
codex plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
codex plugin add compound-engineering@compound-engineering-plugin

steps.title: Use it
steps.text: Call the skill with a mode and your text or a file path: `mode:edit`, `mode:detect` or `mode:author`. In Codex, skills start with `$` instead of `/`.

try.label: A first prompt
try.text: "Check this README for AI writing tells and tell me what to fix, without rewriting it."

watch: It writes a named file in place only when you ask for that. Otherwise it returns the text.
On text that isn't English it applies only the tests, not the pattern list.
If you already have Compound Engineering, the README says to refresh the marketplace before updating, since `/plugin update` alone keeps the old version.

items.name: baoyu-compress-image
items.works_with: Claude Code, Codex and other skills hosts
items.short: Shrinks images to WebP or PNG and picks the best compression tool on your machine for you.
items.what: Point it at an image or a folder and it compresses to WebP by default, or PNG or JPEG, at quality 80 unless you say otherwise. It picks the first tool it finds in this order: sips, cwebp, ImageMagick, then Sharp. It reports the size before and after, like `245KB → 89KB, 64% reduction`.
items.who: Anyone who makes blog posts, sites or docs and wants smaller images without opening an editor. It is one of 20+ skills in the repo, and the author suggests installing only the ones you need.
needs: Node.js, with the ability to run `npx bun` (or Bun installed)

steps.title: Or as a Claude Code plugin
Compress a folder
steps.text: Add `--keep` to keep the originals, and `-f png` to stay in PNG.

watch: By default it replaces the original file. Use `--keep` if you want to keep it.
It can run `npx -y bun` to fetch Bun if you don't have it installed.
Defaults like format and quality can be set in an `EXTEND.md` file in the project or your home config folder.
